title: Distinct Echo Substrings
summary: Calculate the count of unique, non-empty substrings in the given text that can be expressed as the repetition of a substring (a + a where a is any substring).
statement: Calculate the count of unique, non-empty substrings in the given text that can be expressed as the repetition of a substring (a + a where a is any substring).
constraints: text is a nonempty lowercase string.
An echo substring is nonempty and equals some string concatenated with itself.
Count distinct echo substring values, not their number of occurrences.
hints: An echo has an even length and two equal adjacent halves.
Use prefix rolling hashes to compare each pair of halves in constant time.
Try every start and half-length; store the full substring hash together with its length in a set.
Every possible even substring is tested, while the set merges equal echo values from different positions.
editorial: Two prefix hashes make adjacent-half equality and full-substring identity constant-time for each of O(n²) candidates. Including length prevents values of different sizes from sharing an identity. The independent oracle uses direct substring equality and stores actual strings on short seeded inputs.

tests.explanation: The distinct echoes are abcabc, bcabca, and cabcab.
The distinct echo values are aa and aaaa.
